title: Cornish Pasty
subtitle: Hand-crimped pastry filled with beef, turnip, potato and onion
excerpt: The Cornish pasty is the iconic hand-held meal of Cornwall: a thick shortcrust pastry shaped into a D, filled with beef skirt, turnip, potato, and onion, and crimped along the top. It was the meal of the Cornish tin miners who ate the filling from one end and threw away the crimped crust (which their dirty hands had held). Made properly, it is one of the best things you can eat.
sourceNotes: The Cornish pasty has Protected Geographical Indication status in the EU and UK. To be called a Cornish pasty, it must be made in Cornwall, contain skirt beef, turnip (swede), potato and onion, and be crimped on the top. The recipe here can be made outside Cornwall but follows the traditional method. The filling goes in raw -- it cooks inside the pastry.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unbaked. Bake from frozen at 200C for 65 to 70 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch. Freeze the extras unbaked.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry can be made a day ahead.

content.text: The filling goes in raw and cooks inside the sealed pastry. This means the beef must be cut very thinly -- no more than 5 mm -- or it will not cook through. The traditional fat for the pastry is lard. The crimping is done along the top of the D shape, not around the curved edge. A traditional Cornish crimp runs across the top.

items.prepNote: cut into very thin slices then small pieces

content.text: Make the pastry: rub {{lard}} lard and {{unsalted-butter}} butter into {{plain-flour}} flour and {{salt-table}} salt until it resembles breadcrumbs. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time (about 6 to 7 tablespoons) until the dough just comes together. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.

Preheat the oven to 200C. Divide the pastry into 4 equal pieces. Roll each into a circle about 23 cm across. Mix {{potatoes-waxy}} potato, {{swede}} swede, {{beef-skirt}} beef, and {{onion}} onion together. Season well with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper.

Pile a quarter of the filling onto one half of each circle, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold the pastry over to form a D shape. Press the edge firmly to seal. Crimp along the top edge. Brush with beaten {{eggs}} egg. Pierce once with a knife to allow steam to escape.
Place on a baking sheet lined with baking paper. Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until deep golden brown. Rest for at least 10 minutes before eating -- the filling is very hot.

items.symptom: The pastry is pale and the filling is not cooked through
items.cause: The filling slices were too thick, or the oven temperature was too low.
items.fix: Slice the beef very thinly -- it must be thin enough to cook through in the time the pastry takes to colour. If in doubt, return to the oven at 180C for another 15 minutes.

content.text: The Cornish pasty is the most recognisable food from Cornwall. The pasty was the lunch of the tin and copper miners who worked in the mines of west Cornwall from the 16th century until the mines closed in the 20th century. The thick crimped edge served as a handle -- the miners held the pasty by the crimp, ate the filling end, and discarded the crimp because their hands were contaminated with arsenic dust from the ore.
